newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher, intl trade data coming.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher, intl trade data coming.

text.p: U.S. international trade data due before the beginning of trading should determine the stocks market's course at the opening on Wednesday.
Analysts said the tone for the market was slightly positive after yesterday's gains. The Dow rose 50 to about 6398 after flirting with a key psychological level at 6400.
"It looks higher at the opening -- we should see some carry-forward from yesterday and they're buying U.S. stocks in Europe," said Larry Wachtel Prudential Securities analyst.

September U.S. international trade deficit numbers, which indicate U.S. consumers' appetite for foreign products, are due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT from the Commerce Department. Economists expect the shortfall in trade to fall to $9.5 billion from $10.8 billion previously.

"The opening will really depend on the trade number -- if it hits the bond market we could see a lower opening which could move to a reversal later in the day," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"But if it's better than expected and bonds get a pop to the upside, we could reach 6400 on the opening," he said.
Early indicators of the market were slightly negative. The long bond was off 9/32 to yield 6.46 percent and December futures of Standard & Poors 500 Index were off 0.80 to 745.50.
U.S. stocks were mostly higher in London on Wednesday, although traders both in London and in the United States have expressed anxiety over the recent Wall Street buying frenzy.

"To be honest, I would welcome a correction. I don't want to see these gains everyday, and I want to see the broader market participate. It has only been a handful of stocks, which is not very healthy," Cardillo said.
Tokyo stocks closed higher with the Nikkei-225 share index gaining almost 234 to close at 21,190.
London stocks were lower but stable as strong currency fueled worries about a possible interest rate hike there. The FTSE 100 index was off 9.6 to 3968.5.

The dollar moved lower in both European and Asian trading, hurt by comments by Japanese government officials over the strength of the economy invited long-liquidation sales. The greenback was below the key 1.50 mark level.
Shares of Boeing were expected to gain after the company won a $6 billion pact to provide new airplanes to AMR Corp's American Airlines, the Wall Street Journal reported.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column says some analysts have concerns over Citicorp's plan to give performance-based stock options to employees.
Five top officials at Mattel Inc sold more than $38 million worth of option-related stock in late October, just before it announced plans to buy Tyco Toys.
